videos.description: Nova and Sol walk through the RAPP Brainstem: a small, local-first agent server whose core is frozen and pinned by hash, with new capability shipped as drop-in agents. They follow one message from POST /chat through the agent loop, open up a single-file agent, and explain why the core stays frozen. Every factual line is checked against the public kody-w/RAPP source at commit 4084c0e.

card.note: Most agent frameworks want to be your whole stack. Brainstem's core is frozen, pinned by a hash.
card.title: Cold open

card.note: One Python file borrows its model from your GitHub Copilot sign-in; what it can do lives in agents/, one file each.

card.note: A cached soul file, a fresh scan of agents/ on every request, metadata turned into tools, and at most three rounds.

card.note: A BasicAgent subclass with a metadata schema and a perform method that returns a string; a local shim stands in for Azure file storage.
card.title: Anatomy of an agent

card.note: Three files pinned by sha256 to one release; new capability ships as agents, and the RAPP/1 facade lives outside on port 7073.

videos.description: Why would an agent server freeze its own core? Sol answers Nova in about half a minute: three files pinned by sha256 to one release, with new capability shipped as agents around the core, never inside it. Cut from the full episode, Brainstem, explained.
